topic: LLM/agent optimization wizard design inputs for unified-memory NVIDIA devices (DGX Spark GB10 now, RTX Spark N1X next): memory sizing math, fit/throughput estimates at 273 GB/s, runtime flags (vLLM, TRT-LLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, Docker), agent workload needs, misconfiguration detection

facts.claim: DGX Spark hardware envelope: 128 GB unified LPDDR5X, 273 GB/s bandwidth, GB10 with 48 SMs / 6,144 CUDA cores, compute capability sm_121, 20 Arm cores (10 Cortex-X925 + 10 Cortex-A725); ~119-121 GiB visible to the OS after firmware reservations.
facts.detail: Kubesimplify Day 3: '128 GB unified LPDDR5x (approximately 119 GiB usable after firmware reservations)', '273 GB/s (256-bit bus x 8,533 MT/s)', 'sm_121 (consumer/workstation variant, differs from datacenter sm_100)'. Forum benchmark thread reports 'DGX Spark (GB10), 121 GiB unified, Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64, driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0'. LMSYS: 'up to 273 GB/s, shared across both CPU and GPU'.

facts.claim: nvidia-smi does not report memory on GB10; the authoritative headroom number is MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo (or `free -h` 'available' column), not 'free'.
facts.detail: Forum 'Memory Creep' thread: 'nvidia-smi doesn't report memory on GB10 — instead, use /proc/meminfo'. Memory Dashboard thread: 'nvidia-smi memory fields are [N/A] on GB10'. Frank Denneman: nvidia-smi shows 'Not Supported' for the memory bar; 'Use the available column rather than free'. NVIDIA DGX Spark docs list known issue: nvidia-smi reports 'Memory-Usage: Not Supported'. natolambert guide: nvidia-smi shows 'Memory-Usage: N/A'.

facts.claim: Weights memory = params x bytes/param: BF16/FP16 = 2, FP8 = 1, NVFP4 ~0.56 (4-bit values + one FP8 scale per 16-weight block, ~3.5x vs BF16 in practice), MXFP4 ~0.53 (4-bit + shared 8-bit scale per 32-weight block); NVIDIA states NVFP4 checkpoints give ~3.3x disk/GPU-memory reduction vs 16-bit.
facts.detail: Kubesimplify Day 3: 'NVFP4 groups every 16 weights into a block and stores a high-precision FP8 scale factor for the whole block... approximately 3.5x practical compression vs. BF16'. nvidia/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP4 model card: 'reduces the number of bits per parameter from 16 to 4', 'approximately 3.3x' reduction; only linear operators inside transformer blocks are quantized (embeddings/lm_head stay higher precision). gpt-oss cards: 'MXFP4 quantization of the MoE weights' only; attention, router, embeddings, lm_head are not converted (config.json modules_to_not_convert). Worked sizes: gpt-oss-120b (117B) '60+ GB on disk' (Corti); Nemotron-3-Super-120B NVFP4 '~60 GB' checkpoint (Fireworks/HF card via search); Qwen3.6-35B-A3B ollama tags: nvfp4 ~22GB, q4 ~24GB, q8_0 ~39GB, bf16 ~71GB (cli-coding-agent README).

facts.claim: KV cache formula: bytes = 2 (K and V) x num_layers x num_kv_heads x head_dim x context_tokens x bytes_per_element x batch; FP16 = 2 bytes, FP8/q8_0 = 1 byte, q4_0 ~0.5 byte.
facts.detail: Kubesimplify Day 2: 'KV cache size = num_layers x 2 (K and V) x num_kv_heads x head_dim x context_length x bytes_per_element'. Worked (Llama 3.3 70B FP16): 4K ~1.25 GiB, 32K ~10 GiB, 128K ~40 GiB. Ollama docs: q8_0 'approximately half the memory', q4_0 'approximately one-quarter the memory' vs f16.

facts.claim: Per-model attention shapes (from HF config.json) and resulting FP16 KV bytes/token: Llama 3.1 8B: 32 layers, 8 kv heads, head_dim 128 -> 131,072 B (128 KiB)/token -> 4 GiB @32K, 16 GiB @128K. Llama 3.1/3.3 70B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B: 80/8/128 -> 327,680 B (320 KiB)/token -> 10 GiB @32K, 40 GiB @128K. Qwen3-32B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B: 64/8/128 -> 262,144 B (256 KiB)/token -> 8 GiB @32K, 32 GiB @128K. Qwen3-235B-A22B: 94/4/128 -> 192,512 B (188 KiB)/token -> 5.9 GiB @32K, 23.5 GiB @128K.
facts.detail: unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct config: num_hidden_layers 32, num_key_value_heads 8, head_dim 128, max_position_embeddings 131072. unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct: 80, 8, 128, 131072. deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B: 80 layers, 64 heads, 8 kv heads, hidden 8192, 131072. Qwen/Qwen3-32B: 64 layers, 64 heads, 8 kv heads, head_dim 128, max_position_embeddings 40960. deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B: 64 layers, 40 heads, 8 kv heads, hidden 5120 (head_dim 128), 131072. Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B: 94 layers, 64 heads, 4 kv heads, head_dim 128, 128 experts, 8 per token, 40960. Arithmetic done by me from these values.

facts.claim: gpt-oss shapes: gpt-oss-120b = 36 layers, 8 kv heads, head_dim 64, 128 experts / 4 active, 117B total / 5.1B active, 131072 max positions, alternating sliding_window 128 layers; gpt-oss-20b = 24 layers, 8 kv heads, head_dim 64, 32 experts / 4 active, 21B total / 3.6B active. Upper-bound FP16 KV: 120b = 73,728 B (72 KiB)/token (9 GiB @128K); 20b = 49,152 B (48 KiB)/token (6 GiB @128K); real usage is lower because half the layers are sliding-window (128 tokens).
facts.detail: openai/gpt-oss-120b config.json: num_hidden_layers 36, num_key_value_heads 8, head_dim 64, num_local_experts 128, num_experts_per_tok 4, sliding_window 128, quant_method mxfp4. Model card: '117B parameters with 5.1B active parameters', runs 'on a single 80GB GPU'. gpt-oss-20b config: 24 layers, 8 kv, head_dim 64, 32 experts; card: '21B parameters with 3.6B active parameters', 'run within 16GB of memory'.

facts.claim: Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B (NVFP4 checkpoint) is a hybrid Mamba-2/MoE with only 8 attention layers out of 88, 2 kv heads, head_dim 128, 512 routed experts + 1 shared, 22 experts/token, 262,144 max positions; attention KV is tiny (~8 KiB/token FP16) but Ollama allocates ~7 GB per parallel slot at 262K context, and in-memory footprint via Ollama is ~94 GB leaving ~27 GiB headroom.
facts.detail: HF config.json: num_hidden_layers 88, hybrid_override_pattern 'MEMEMEM*EMEMEMEM*EMEMEMEM*EMEMEMEMEM*EMEMEMEMEM*EMEMEMEMEM*EMEMEMEMEM*EMEMEMEM*EMEMEMEME' (8 '*' attention layers), num_key_value_heads 2, head_dim 128, n_routed_experts 512, num_experts_per_tok 22, max_position_embeddings 262144; quantization group 0 = FP8 for attention/shared expert, group 1 = FP4 group_size 16 for routed experts. Frank Denneman: 'Nemotron 3 Super (120B): Downloads 86 GB, In-memory 94 GB, Headroom remaining ~27 GiB'; 'Approximately 7 GB per parallel request slot at 262K context length'; Nemotron 3 Nano 30B: 24 GB download, 27 GB in memory, ~89 GiB headroom.

facts.claim: Bandwidth-bound decode estimate: tokens/s ~= 273 GB/s / bytes read per token (active weights + KV). Published theoretical maxima: Llama 3.1 8B Q4 (4.5 GB) ~61 tok/s; Llama 3.3 70B NVFP4 (40 GB) ~6.8 tok/s; gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 (~3.6 GB active) ~75 tok/s; Nemotron 3 Super 120B NVFP4 (~6 GB active) ~45 tok/s. Measured numbers land at roughly 50-80% of these.
facts.detail: Kubesimplify Day 2: '273 GB/s memory bandwidth divided by your model's bytes in memory ~ your decode tok/s' with the table above. Measured comparisons: LMSYS SGLang Llama 3.1 8B FP8 batch 1 = 20.5 tok/s decode (theoretical ~34 for 8 GB weights); Llama 3.1 70B FP8 = 2.7 tok/s (theoretical ~3.9); gpt-oss-120b 50-60 tok/s; Nemotron 3 Super NVFP4 22.7-23.7 tok/s (vLLM blog) to ~38 tok/s (Kubesimplify).

facts.claim: LMSYS published DGX Spark benchmarks (Oct 2025): SGLang Llama 3.1 8B FP8 batch 1 = 7,991 tok/s prefill / 20.5 tok/s decode, batch 32 = 7,949 / 368; Ollama gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 = 2,053 / 49.7; SGLang DeepSeek-R1 14B FP8 batch 8 = 2,074 / 83.5; Llama 3.1 70B FP8 decodes ~2.7 tok/s; EAGLE3 speculative decoding gave up to 2x. Follow-up post: gpt-oss-20b ~70 tok/s and gpt-oss-120b ~50 tok/s with SGLang (lmsysorg/sglang:spark).
facts.detail: LMSYS review states DGX Spark 'excels at prompt processing' but 'struggles with token generation — the memory-bandwidth-bound phase'. gpt-oss post docker command: 'docker run --gpus all --shm-size 32g -p 30000:30000 ... --ipc=host lmsysorg/sglang:spark python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path openai/gpt-oss-20b --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --reasoning-parser gpt-oss --tool-call-parser gpt-oss'; notes 'Optional: Enable swap memory for GPT-OSS 120B stability'.

facts.claim: Same-harness single-Spark benchmark (vLLM 0.26.1rc1, driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0): gpt-oss-120b Ollama 42.1 tok/s single / 42.5 at 8 concurrent (no batching gain) vs vLLM 60.7 single / 116-153 aggregate; Qwen3-30B-A3B Ollama 85.2 vs vLLM 77.1 single / 313.4 aggregate; Gemma-4-26B-A4B NVFP4+MTP vLLM 54.9 single / 303.6 aggregate; ~6,000 tok/s prefill vs ~56 tok/s generation typical; MTP speculative decoding gave +81% (30.3 -> 54.9).
facts.detail: Forum post by a community member, data published. Key wizard-relevant finding: 'Ollama showed no batching behavior — concurrent throughput matched single-stream performance across all four models tested'; TTFT 94-511 ms for ~short prompts.

facts.claim: Concurrency scaling on a single Spark (Dendro Logic, vLLM 26.03, ~1,500-token prompts, 400 output): gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 33.5 tok/s at c=1 -> 862.8 aggregate at c=256 (3.6 per seq); Nemotron Super 49B NVFP4 5.8 -> 695 at c=256; Nemotron Nano 9B v2 plateaus ~155 aggregate after c=8; gpt-oss-120b used ~9% KV at c=256; dual-model production stack ~85 GB total leaving 30+ GB headroom.
facts.detail: Flags used: '--max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 --enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code -e VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4=1 -e VLLM_FLASHINFER_MOE_BACKEND=throughput'. Aggregate throughput fell beyond c=256 (320: 514; 384: 771 for gpt-oss).

facts.claim: vLLM team's official DGX Spark guidance (June 2026): --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 ('leave room for the operating system, kernel page cache, container runtime, KV cache growth'), --max-model-len 131072, --max-num-seqs 4 ('above this, bandwidth overhead outweighs batching gains'), leave --kv-cache-dtype unset for stability (fp8 only under memory pressure), leave --quantization unset for pre-quantized NVFP4 checkpoints; recommended class is '100-130B MoE NVFP4 models with roughly 10-15 billion active parameters'; Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 measured 22.7-23.7 tok/s decode, TTFT 0.42 s @58 tokens / 3.85 s @7,234 tokens; first request after startup ~25 s JIT warm-up; first load 10-15 min.
facts.detail: Exact command: 'docker run -d --name vllm --ipc=host --restart unless-stopped --gpus all -p 8000:8000 -e HF_TOKEN="$HF_TOKEN" -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 --served-model-name nemotron-3-super --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-num-seqs 4 --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder'. Readiness: 'curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/models | jq -r .data[0].id'. KV utilization 'below 5% during single-user tests and below 30% under small-batch demo traffic'.

facts.claim: vLLM's default --gpu-memory-utilization is 0.92 and it is 'The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model executor'; on GB10 that fraction is taken of the whole unified pool, so the default pre-allocates ~110 GiB and starves the OS. --max-model-len 'If unspecified, will be automatically derived from the model config' (e.g. 262144 for Qwen3.6/Nemotron), which inflates pre-allocated KV.
facts.detail: vLLM engine args docs: default 0.92; --kv-cache-dtype options 'auto, bfloat16, float16, fp8, fp8_e4m3, fp8_e5m2'; --enforce-eager disables CUDA graphs; --cpu-offload-gb default 0. Forum 'Memory creep' worked example: default vLLM config consumed 117 GB (weights 19 GB, runtime 3 GB, torch.compile + CUDA graphs 13 GB, pre-allocated KV 89 GB) vs optimized 32 GB with '--enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8' and env 'VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4=0 VLLM_NVFP4_GEMM_BACKEND=marlin VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1'.

facts.claim: NVIDIA vLLM playbook for DGX Spark uses nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.05-py3 with 'docker run -it --gpus all -p 8000:8000 nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.05-py3 vllm serve ${HF_MODEL_HANDLE}'; per-model recipes span --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4-0.9, --max-model-len 2048-262144, --kv-cache-dtype fp8, --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN or flashinfer, --max-num-seqs 4-10; prerequisites are CUDA 13.0 toolkit (nvcc --version), docker, python3.12, NVIDIA Container Toolkit; OOM fix is 'Reduce --max-model-len and --max-num-seqs'.
facts.detail: Also lists vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-cu130 and vllm/vllm-openai:latest. Kubesimplify warns: 'The exact Docker image tag determines kernel support for ARM64 and Blackwell GB10 (sm_121). Mutable tags like latest can silently run outdated builds.'

facts.claim: vLLM kernel-init on GB10 can allocate ~50 GB (FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, NVFP4-Cutlass, FlashInfer-Cutlass MoE, TritonAttn) before weights load; with a 75 GB NVFP4 checkpoint available RAM dropped from ~120.9 GB to 68.5 GB then 44.6 GB, which trips 'Auto-prefetch is disabled... checkpoint size exceeds 90% of available RAM' and slows loading by minutes.
facts.detail: Container nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.07-py3 on 121 GB unified. Wizard implication: budget 10-15 GB for runtime/JIT/cudagraph on top of weights + KV, and warn when weights > ~0.6 x MemAvailable for vLLM.

facts.claim: Exhausting unified memory on DGX Spark tends to freeze the whole OS (SSH dead, HDMI black, hard power cycle) rather than OOM-kill the process; swap makes it worse ('when the swap is being used, the system becomes unresponsive'); community fix is to disable swap so 'the process will just exit, but leaves you with a running system', plus vm.swappiness=0/1, vm.min_free_kbytes=2097152, drop_caches before loading.
facts.detail: Crash thread: crashes at docker --memory=110G/90G/30G limits because 'this parameter can only limit the memory (RAM), not the GPU's VRAM'; kernel 6.14.0-1013-nvidia aarch64. Stability thread: freeze at 126.5 GB used (~1.5 GB free); example need 73.40GiB (weights 29.40GiB + KV 40.00GiB + safety 4GiB) vs 90.39GiB free of 115.39GiB; commands 'sudo sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0', 'sudo sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=2097152', 'sudo sysctl -w vm.vfs_cache_pressure=200', 'sudo swapoff -a'. natolambert: 'sudo swapoff -a; swapon --show # should print nothing'. Memory-creep thread: 'sudo sysctl vm.swappiness=1', 'sudo sysctl vm.dirty_bytes=268435456', 'sudo sh -c sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches', 'sudo systemctl set-default multi-user.target' saves 2-3 GB.

facts.claim: Thermal/power: DGX Spark firmware can cause sudden shutdowns under heavy inference; community workaround is to lock GPU clocks at 2150 MHz ('nvidia-smi -lgc 200,2150' or 'nvidia-smi --lock-gpu-clocks 0,2150', ~1-2% perf cost). ACPI/TSOC ~95 C triggers reboot. GPU max draw 120 W, rest of system 100 W, PSU 240 W; nvidia-smi -pl returns N/A (no user power cap). Healthy load shows ~35-100 W; 100 W plateau with sw_thermal_slowdown Active = thermal cap; ~4.8 W with ~0% util = PD-controller 27 W defect (dmesg 'Detected insufficient power on the PCIe slot (27W)') or the 5 W bug fixed by driver 580.x/CUDA 13.
facts.detail: NVIDIA staff quote: 'Spark GPU can draw a max of 120W and the rest of the system including CPU, CX7 and peripherals can draw 100W. The power supply is rated for 240 Watt of peak draw.' Detection command: 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw,temperature.gpu,clocks.throttle_reasons.sw_thermal_slowdown --format=csv,noheader'; healthy sample '35.65 W, 96 %, 2522 MHz'; defective '4.80 W, 2 %, 2411 MHz'. Firmware update reduced OS boot memory from 14 GB to 3 GB.

facts.claim: Prebuilt CUDA-12 PyTorch/vLLM wheels do not work on DGX OS (CUDA 13 only): 'ImportError: libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory'. Correct install is the cu130 index: 'pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130'. PyTorch prints 'Found GPU0 NVIDIA GB10 which is of cuda capability 12.1. Minimum and Maximum cuda capability supported by this version of PyTorch is (8.0) - (12.0)' which is safe to ignore because sm_120 cubins run on sm_121. Triton needs 'export TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas' to avoid 'ptxas fatal : Value sm_121a is not defined for option gpu-name'. Do not pip install flash-attn on GB10.
facts.detail: natolambert/dgx-spark-setup and TRT-LLM 1.3.0rc5 forum thread ('triton.runtime.errors.PTXASError: PTXAS error: Internal Triton PTX codegen error', fix 'mpirun -x TRITON_PTXAS_PATH'). vLLM issue #31128: vLLM 0.13 pinned torch==2.9.0 with no aarch64 CUDA wheels; NGC PyTorch 25.11 ships 2.10; closed via PR #37700. Issue #36821: 'vLLM fails to start on NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10 Blackwell, sm_121) because the bundled PyTorch binary only includes compiled CUDA kernels through sm_120'; runtime TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST/LD_LIBRARY_PATH 'have no effect on prebuilt binaries'.

facts.claim: Missing native Blackwell cubins in a vLLM build silently costs ~4x decode speed: stock vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly (v0.17.0rc1, Mar 2026) gave 13 tok/s on Qwen3.5-35B vs 48.6 tok/s after rebuilding _C.abi3.so/_moe_C.abi3.so with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.1"; detect with 'cuobjdump -lelf _C.abi3.so | grep -c sm_120' (0 = bad, 50+ = good). SM121 lacks the cvt.e2m1x2 instruction so NVFP4 microscaling kernels fail with 'ptxas error: Instruction cvt with .e2m1x2 not supported on .target sm_121'.
facts.detail: Build env: TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.1", VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda, VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1, MAX_JOBS=4; CMake pattern '12.0f' -> '12.0a' patch. eugr/spark-vllm-docker adds: 'Driver 590.x has CUDAGraph capture deadlock on GB10'; 'NVFP4 models: not fully supported on vLLM yet; performance suboptimal' (as of that README); env PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True, VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0, DG_JIT_USE_NVRTC=0.

facts.claim: llama.cpp on GB10 must be built with CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121 (or 121a / 121a-real); building for 120 yields 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device'. NVIDIA playbook build: 'cmake -B build -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_CURL=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121a-real' then 'cmake --build build --config Release --target llama-server -j'. Correct build logs 'compute capability 12.1'. ggml maintainers' one-liner: 'bash <(curl -s https://ggml.ai/dgx-spark.sh)'. GCC 13.3 + CUDA 13.0 build failures need NVIDIA's nvcc (not Ubuntu's nvidia-cuda-toolkit) or GCC 12.
facts.detail: llama.cpp discussion #16514 and NVIDIA/dgx-spark-playbooks/nvidia/llama-cpp. Playbook run: './bin/llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000' (~30 GB RAM), MTP: '--chat-template-kwargs {"preserve_thinking": true} --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3'; OOM fix 'Lower --ctx-size or use a smaller quantization'; CUDA not found fix 'export PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH'; health 'curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:30000/health'. ggerganov perf thread: gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 pp2048 ~1,956 t/s, tg32 ~60 t/s, falling to ~40 t/s at 32K depth; bench cmd 'llama-bench -m model.gguf -fa 1 -d 0,4096,8192,16384,32768 -p 2048 -n 32 -ub 2048 -mmp 0'; 'NVIDIA 6.17.1 kernel with NO_PAGE_MAPCOUNT' needed for fast model loading.

facts.claim: llama.cpp runtime flags used on Spark: '-ngl 999 -fa on --no-mmap --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 -b 2048 -ub 2048 -c 65536 --jinja' (vlaicu playbook) and '-c 16384 -ngl 999 --flash-attn on --no-mmap --kv-unified --jinja -ub 2048' for gpt-oss-120b (Corti). --no-mmap works around a known mmap slow-load issue on Spark (~5x load inflation). Allowed -ctk/-ctv values: f32, f16, bf16, q8_0, q4_0, q4_1, iq4_nl, q5_0, q5_1 (default f16); -fa on/off/auto (default auto); -c default 0 = from model; -ngl accepts number, 'auto', 'all'.
facts.detail: llama.cpp server README help text. Corti: throughput 'dropped from ~20-25 tok/s at 16K context to ~15-17 tok/s at 32K' for their config; weights '60+ GB on disk'. vlaicu: 'Keep at q8_0 or higher' for KV; error strings 'couldn't bind HTTP server socket, port: N', 'unknown model architecture: gemma4-assistant'.

facts.claim: Ollama env vars and defaults: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH default 4096; OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL default 1 (memory scales with it); OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS default 3 x GPUs; OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE f16 (default) | q8_0 (~half) | q4_0 (~quarter), applies globally; OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1/0; OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE; OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE default 512; set via 'systemctl edit ollama.service' -> [Service] Environment="VAR=value"; per-request num_ctx in options. 'ollama ps' PROCESSOR column: '100% GPU' = fully on GPU, '100% CPU' = system memory, '48%/52% CPU/GPU' = split.
facts.detail: Ollama docs FAQ. Ollama issue #13337: KV cache quantization only honored for architectures with flash attention support (gemma3, gptoss, mistral3, qwen3/qwen3moe, qwen3vl); otherwise 'the server silently falls back to f16, leading to unexpected OOMs'. Issue #15043: with OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 + OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 on unsupported models: 'V cache quantization requires flash_attn' then 'panic: unable to create llama context'. On unified memory the CPU/GPU split reading is less meaningful for headroom but non-'100% GPU' still means slower llama.cpp CPU path.

facts.claim: NVIDIA CLI coding agent playbook (Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex CLI via Ollama) uses Qwen3.6 tags: 'qwen3.6' (35B-A3B MoE, ~24GB), 'qwen3.6:35b-a3b-nvfp4' (~22GB), 'qwen3.6:35b-a3b-q8_0' (~39GB), 'qwen3.6:35b-a3b-bf16' (~71GB); 'Qwen3.6 ships with a 256K context window by default'; requires DGX OS 7.3.1 (Ubuntu 24.04.3) and Ollama v0.15+; commands 'ollama pull qwen3.6', 'ollama launch claude --model qwen3.6', 'ollama launch opencode --model qwen3.6', 'ollama launch codex --model qwen3.6'.
facts.detail: Troubleshooting strings: 'ollama: command not found', 'ollama launch unknown command' -> update to v0.15+, 'Connection refused to localhost:11434', CUDA context destroyed (multi-GPU) -> 'CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0'. Corti routes Claude Code to llama.cpp with 'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8005'.

facts.claim: NemoClaw on DGX Spark: installer 'curl -fsSL https://www.nvidia.com/nemoclaw.sh | bash'; prerequisites Ubuntu 24.04, Docker 28.x+, Node.js 22.16+; default express-install model 'qwen3.6-35b-a3b-nvfp4' on managed local vLLM at http://127.0.0.1:8000 (verify 'curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models'); ports 18789-18790 dashboard, 8080 gateway, 8000 vLLM; OpenShell embeds k3s in Docker and needs '/etc/docker/daemon.json' -> {"default-cgroupns-mode": "host"} on cgroup v2 or kubelet fails with 'Failed to start ContainerManager: failed to initialize top level QOS containers'; sandbox has no direct GPU access, inference is routed via host-side provider.
facts.detail: dgx-spark-playbooks/nvidia/nemoclaw README + NemoClaw dev guide. Troubleshooting: 'nemoclaw: command not found' -> source ~/.bashrc; 'Docker permission denied' -> 'sudo usermod -aG docker $USER'; 'Port 18789 already in use' -> 'lsof -i :18789'; 'origin not allowed' -> use http://127.0.0.1; CoreDNS crash loop -> re-run installer. Cgroup check 'stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup/'. Policy tiers Balanced/Restricted/Open.

facts.claim: NVIDIA's agent-scaling guidance for DGX Spark: agents commonly use 30K-120K token contexts ('Large context windows of 30K-250K tokens are processed efficiently'); running four concurrent subagents on 32K inputs 'requires only 2.6x more time' vs one; Nemotron 120B processed a single 128K-token prompt at 2,855 tok/s (44 s prefill); recommended models Nemotron 3 Super 120B, Qwen3.5 35B, Qwen3 Coder Next 80B, Llama 3.3 70B; TRT-LLM/vLLM/SGLang for concurrency.
facts.detail: NVIDIA developer blog. Implication for wizard: agent profiles should size KV for >=64K-128K context x (1 + number of subagents) and prefer MoE NVFP4/MXFP4 with 3-15B active params. Kubesimplify Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (30B-A3B, 52 layers, 262,144 default context, 26 GB resident via Ollama, ~86 GB headroom): Ollama 72-87 tok/s, vLLM NVFP4 95-108 tok/s; 'Lightning required 485 tokens in 5.9 seconds versus competing model's 1,953 tokens in 26 seconds' on a tool-calling task.

facts.claim: NVIDIA TRT-LLM playbook for Spark: image nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc13; docker flags '--gpus all --ipc host --network host --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 -v $HOME/.cache/huggingface/:/root/.cache/huggingface/ -e HF_TOKEN=$HF_TOKEN'; models nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP4, nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16, openai/gpt-oss-20b, nvidia/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP4 (multi-node only); KV via YAML 'free_gpu_memory_fraction: 0.9'; OOM fix 'Reduce free_gpu_memory_fraction: 0.9 or batch size'; 'export TRT_LLM_DISABLE_LOAD_WEIGHTS_IN_PARALLEL=1' for memory pressure during load.
facts.detail: SGLang playbook: image lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130, launch '--trust-remote-code --tp 1 --attention-backend flashinfer --mem-fraction-static 0.75', 'for NVFP4 models, add the --quantization modelopt_fp4 flag', warns unified memory 'may cause issues even when within the memory capacity, requiring manual cache clearing'. Forum: TRT-LLM NVFP4 safetensors reported slower than LM Studio GGUF on Spark in early 2026; Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP4 (133B-param checkpoint incl. overhead) is listed multi-node only.

facts.claim: Recent (mid-2026) dense-model reality on Spark: Qwen3.8-27B FP8 via vLLM decodes 8.2 tok/s single (57.9 aggregate at c=10); NVFP4 11.5 single / 84.3 aggregate; llama.cpp Q4_K_XL 11.6 tok/s; Ollama Q4_K_M with MTP 26.5 tok/s; recipe 'gpu_memory_utilization: 0.8, max_model_len: 131072, attention_backend: flashinfer, kv_cache_dtype: fp8'; FP8 'wedged under 10 concurrent requests at 32K context'; 'Must stop prior inference servers before launching new ones due to unified memory pooling'; MTP nightly caused 'hard reboots at 16K context depth with 2 concurrent requests'.
facts.detail: Kubesimplify (driver 580.159.03, kernel 6.17.0-1018-nvidia, ~121.7 GB usable). Also Gemma 4 31B NVFP4 vLLM: 6.15 tok/s single -> 92.1 aggregate at 16 concurrent; Qwen2.5-3B BF16 26 -> 1,462 tok/s at 64 concurrent; engine overhead on same GGUF: llama.cpp 101.6 vs Ollama 93.7 vs Docker Model Runner 99.1 tok/s.

detection_heuristics.what: Unified-memory platform detection (GB10 / N1X) and correct headroom source
detection_heuristics.how: Linux: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name --format=csv,noheader contains 'GB10'; /proc/device-tree/model or dmidecode product contains 'DGX Spark' / 'GB10'; nvidia-smi memory.used/memory.total query returns '[N/A]' or 'Not Supported'. Read /proc/meminfo MemTotal and MemAvailable (expect MemTotal ~121 GiB on 128 GB Spark). Never use nvidia-smi memory or 'free' column for headroom. Windows (RTX Spark): PCI VEN_10DE&DEV_2E03 or DEV_2E06, driver >= 616.00, OS architecture ARM64; use GlobalMemoryStatusEx ullAvailPhys.
exact_strings: NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X (6144-core Blackwell RTX GPU)
NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X (5120-core Blackwell RTX GPU)

detection_heuristics.what: Swap or zram enabled on a unified-memory box (OS freeze risk under memory pressure)
detection_heuristics.how: Run 'swapon --show' (non-empty = swap active) or parse /proc/swaps for any line beyond the header; check for /dev/zram* entries and 'zramswap' or 'systemd-zram-setup@' units via systemctl; read /proc/sys/vm/swappiness (>1 is WARN if swap present).
exact_strings: when the swap is being used, the system becomes unresponsive

detection_heuristics.what: CUDA-12 Python wheels on a CUDA-13-only DGX OS (torch/vllm/flash-attn built for cu12)
detection_heuristics.how: pip show torch | grep Version and match suffix '+cu12'; python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda)' starts with '12.'; scan pip freeze for nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12 / nvidia-cublas-cu12; ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12* absent; grep service/container logs for the ImportError string. Correct state: torch.version.cuda '13.x' and wheel index cu130.
exact_strings: ImportError: libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

detection_heuristics.what: CPU-only torch or GPU not visible to torch
detection_heuristics.how: python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_capability())' expecting True and (12, 1); torch.__version__ containing '+cpu' is CRIT; also check 'python -c "import torch;print(torch.cuda.get_arch_list())"' contains 'sm_120' or 'sm_121' (sm_120 cubins run on sm_121).
exact_strings: Found GPU0 NVIDIA GB10 which is of cuda capability 12.1. Minimum and Maximum cuda capability supported by this version of PyTorch is (8.0) - (12.0)

detection_heuristics.what: Kernels built for the wrong architecture (sm_121 missing) in llama.cpp, vLLM, Triton, TRT-LLM
detection_heuristics.how: grep server/container logs for the runtime error strings below; for llama.cpp verify build log/`llama-server --version`/startup log mentions 'compute capability 12.1' and that the cmake cache (build/CMakeCache.txt) has CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121, 121a or 121a-real (120 = bad); for vLLM in a container run 'cuobjdump -lelf $(python -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__))")/_C.abi3.so | grep -c sm_120' and treat 0 as missing native Blackwell cubins; for Triton/TRT-LLM check TRITON_PTXAS_PATH is set to /usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas when the ptxas error appears.
exact_strings: no kernel image is available for execution on the device
ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_121a' is not defined for option 'gpu-name'
triton.runtime.errors.PTXASError: PTXAS error: Internal Triton PTX codegen error
ptxas error: Instruction 'cvt with .e2m1x2' not supported on .target 'sm_121'

detection_heuristics.what: vLLM memory misconfiguration on unified memory (default 0.92 utilization, auto max-model-len, no headroom)
detection_heuristics.how: Inspect running vLLM process cmdline (ps -eo args | grep 'vllm serve' or docker inspect Cmd): flag --gpu-memory-utilization absent (default 0.92) or > 0.85 -> WARN; --max-model-len absent (auto = model max, e.g. 262144) -> WARN; compute planned bytes = gpu_mem_util x MemTotal and compare with MemAvailable minus 8 GiB OS floor; grep logs for OOM and the auto-prefetch message; suggest --kv-cache-dtype fp8 and --max-num-seqs 4 when over budget.
exact_strings: checkpoint size exceeds 90% of available RAM
The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model executor

detection_heuristics.what: Ollama KV-cache/flash-attention misconfiguration and model spill to CPU
detection_heuristics.how: Read env from 'systemctl show ollama -p Environment' or /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/*.conf: if OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE is q8_0/q4_0 and OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION is not 1, WARN; grep journalctl -u ollama for the panic string; run 'ollama ps' and parse PROCESSOR column, anything other than '100% GPU' -> WARN; parse CONTEXT column and compute KV bytes = ctx x OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL x per-token bytes; if OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH unset, note default 4096 (too small for agents) unless model ships 256K default.
exact_strings: panic: unable to create llama context

detection_heuristics.what: Two or more heavy inference servers resident at once on the shared pool
detection_heuristics.how: Enumerate listeners with 'ss -ltnp' for 8000 (vLLM/NemoClaw), 30000 (SGLang/llama.cpp playbook), 11434 (Ollama), 8080/8005 (llama.cpp), 8355 (trtllm-serve) plus 'docker ps' images matching vllm|sglang|tensorrt-llm|llama.cpp|ollama; sum RSS of those processes (or /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS) and 'ollama ps' SIZE; if two servers each > 20 GiB or combined > 0.7 x MemTotal -> WARN; Kubesimplify explicitly: 'Must stop prior inference servers before launching new ones due to unified memory pooling'.

detection_heuristics.what: Power/thermal cap or defect limiting throughput
detection_heuristics.how: Sample 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw,utilization.gpu,clocks.sm,temperature.gpu,clocks.throttle_reasons.sw_thermal_slowdown,clocks.throttle_reasons.hw_slowdown --format=csv,noheader' during a short load; power ~5 W with util <5% under load = CRIT (PD defect or old driver); power plateau ~100 W with sw_thermal_slowdown 'Active' or temp >= 85 C = WARN; dmesg for the PCIe power string; 'nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK' locked at 2150 MHz indicates user workaround in place (INFO); nvidia-smi -pl returns N/A so no power-cap check is possible via that path.
exact_strings: Detected insufficient power on the PCIe slot (27W)

detection_heuristics.how: docker inspect <container> and check HostConfig: IpcMode == 'host' or ShmSize >= 16 GiB (LMSYS uses --shm-size 32g, forum 30G); Ulimits contains memlock -1 (TRT-LLM playbook) ; DeviceRequests includes gpus all or Runtime nvidia; if --memory limit set, INFO that it cannot bound GPU allocations ('this parameter can only limit the memory (RAM), not the GPU's VRAM'). Mutable tag ':latest' on vllm/sglang images -> INFO (silently outdated sm_121 kernels).

detection_heuristics.what: Desktop session and page cache eating headroom before a large load
detection_heuristics.how: 'systemctl get-default' == graphical.target and a logged-in GNOME session -> INFO (2-3 GB); compute Cached+Buffers from /proc/meminfo and suggest 'sudo sh -c "sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches"' before loading a model whose weights exceed MemAvailable but not MemAvailable+Cached; kernel version < 6.17.1 -> INFO about slow model load (NO_PAGE_MAPCOUNT); driver 590.x -> WARN (vLLM CUDAGraph deadlock report).

node --version >= 22.16; docker info --format '{{.ServerVersion}}' 28.x; /etc/docker/daemon.json contains "default-cgroupns-mode": "host"; 'stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup/' == cgroup2fs; ports 18789, 18790, 8080, 8000 free or owned by nemoclaw/vllm; 'curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models' returns the served model; kubelet error string in openshell logs indicates cgroup fix missing.
exact_strings: Failed to start ContainerManager: failed to initialize top level QOS containers

candidate_rules.trigger: Planned footprint (weights + KV(ctx x parallel x bytes/token) + runtime reserve 8-15 GiB) exceeds MemAvailable, or vLLM --gpu-memory-utilization x MemTotal > MemAvailable - 8 GiB
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Plan needs {need_gib} GiB (weights {w_gib} + KV {kv_gib} @ {ctx} ctx x {par} seqs + runtime {rt_gib}) but MemAvailable is {avail_gib} GiB of {total_gib} GiB; on GB10 this freezes the OS rather than OOM-killing.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: On unified memory there is no separate VRAM; exhaustion locks the machine (SSH dead, black HDMI, power-cycle). Forum reports crashes at 126.5 GB used.
next_steps: Reduce context (--max-model-len / -c / num_ctx) or parallelism (--max-num-seqs / -np / OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL)
Use FP8/q8_0 KV cache (--kv-cache-dtype fp8, --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0, OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 with OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1)
Pick a smaller quant (NVFP4/MXFP4/Q4) or a MoE model with fewer total params
Stop other resident model servers first

candidate_rules.trigger: swapon --show non-empty or /dev/zram* present on a GB10/N1X unified-memory host
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Swap active: {swap_devices} ({swap_size}); vm.swappiness={swappiness}. Community guidance for DGX Spark is to disable swap so a runaway model exits instead of freezing the system.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: When the shared pool spills to swap/zram the whole box becomes unresponsive; disabling swap converts a hang into a process crash.
next_steps: sudo swapoff -a && swapon --show  # should print nothing
Comment swap entries in /etc/fstab; disable zram units
sudo sysctl -w vm.swappiness=1 vm.min_free_kbytes=2097152 (persist in /etc/sysctl.conf)

candidate_rules.trigger: vLLM running without --gpu-memory-utilization (default 0.92) or with value > 0.85, or without explicit --max-model-len, on unified memory
candidate_rules.evidence_template: vLLM cmdline: {cmdline}. gpu-memory-utilization={util} reserves {util_gib} GiB of the {total_gib} GiB shared pool, leaving {left_gib} GiB for OS/page cache/other services. max-model-len={mml} (auto = model max) pre-allocates {kv_gib} GiB KV.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: vLLM's fraction is taken from the same pool the OS runs in; a default config was measured at 117 GB (89 GB pre-allocated KV) vs 32 GB when tuned. The vLLM team's Spark guidance is 0.85 / 131072 / --max-num-seqs 4.
next_steps: Set --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6-0.85 sized to weights + desired KV + 8 GiB floor
Set --max-model-len to the real need (e.g. 65536 or 131072) and --max-num-seqs 4 (agents) to 8-16 (batch APIs)
Add --kv-cache-dtype fp8 only if still over budget; consider --enforce-eager to drop CUDA-graph memory (slower)

candidate_rules.trigger: torch.version.cuda starts with '12.' or wheel tag +cu12x, or logs contain libcudart.so.12 ImportError, on DGX OS (CUDA 13 only)
candidate_rules.evidence_template: torch {torch_version} built for CUDA {torch_cuda} but host has CUDA {host_cuda} and no libcudart.so.12; error seen: 'ImportError: libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file'.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: CUDA 12 wheels cannot load on CUDA-13-only DGX OS; runtimes silently fall back to CPU or fail to start.
next_steps: pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130
Prefer NGC/official arm64 cu130 containers (nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.05-py3, vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly)
Do not pip install flash-attn on GB10; use SDPA/FlashInfer bundled by the runtime

candidate_rules.trigger: torch.__version__ contains '+cpu' or torch.cuda.is_available() is False on a host where nvidia-smi sees GB10
candidate_rules.evidence_template: torch {torch_version}: cuda.is_available()={avail}; GPU 'NVIDIA GB10' present. Expected capability (12, 1).
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Silent CPU inference on a 20-core Arm CPU is 10-50x slower than the GPU path and burns the shared memory pool twice.
next_steps: Reinstall torch from the cu130 index
Verify: python -c 'import torch;print(torch.cuda.get_device_capability())' -> (12, 1)

candidate_rules.trigger: Runtime logs contain 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device', 'sm_121a is not defined', or 'cvt with .e2m1x2 not supported'; or llama.cpp CMakeCache has CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120; or vLLM _C.abi3.so has zero sm_120 cubins
candidate_rules.evidence_template: {runtime} built without native Blackwell (sm_121) kernels: {evidence}. Measured impact on Spark: 13 tok/s vs 48.6 tok/s for Qwen3.5-35B after rebuild.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Wrong-arch builds either fail outright or fall back to slow generic/PTX paths, costing up to 4x decode throughput.
next_steps: llama.cpp: rebuild with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121 (or 121a-real); confirm 'compute capability 12.1' in startup log
Triton/TRT-LLM: export TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas
vLLM: use a recent cu130 arm64 image; verify cuobjdump -lelf _C.abi3.so | grep -c sm_120 > 0

candidate_rules.trigger: OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0|q4_0 without OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1, or model architecture not in the flash-attention allowlist, or 'ollama ps' PROCESSOR != '100% GPU'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Ollama env: KV_CACHE_TYPE={kv} FLASH_ATTENTION={fa}; ollama ps: {model} PROCESSOR='{proc}' CONTEXT={ctx} SIZE={size}. Quantized KV silently falls back to f16 (or panics: 'V cache quantization requires flash_attn') when flash attention is unavailable.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Memory plans built on q8_0 KV are wrong by 2x if the runtime falls back to f16; a CPU/GPU split means the llama.cpp CPU path is in use.
next_steps: Set Environment="OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1" and Environment="OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0" via systemctl edit ollama.service, then systemctl restart ollama
Use models with FA support (gemma3, gptoss, mistral3, qwen3/qwen3moe, qwen3vl) or accept f16 KV in the budget
Check num_ctx / OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH: default 4096 is too small for coding agents; Qwen3.6 ships 256K by default

candidate_rules.trigger: Two or more model servers (vLLM :8000, SGLang :30000, Ollama :11434 with loaded models, llama-server, trtllm-serve) resident with combined RSS/model size > 70% of MemTotal, or OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS default 3 with large models
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Resident servers: {servers_with_gib}. Combined {sum_gib} GiB of {total_gib} GiB; MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Every server carves from the same 121 GiB; vLLM's pre-allocation plus an Ollama model can exceed the pool without any single process looking oversized.
next_steps: Stop the server you are not using (systemctl stop ollama / docker stop vllm)
Set OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 and OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE appropriately
Use a router (llama-swap/LiteLLM) to load/unload instead of co-residency

candidate_rules.trigger: Under load GPU power ~5 W with util < 5% (CRIT), or power plateau ~100 W with clocks.throttle_reasons.sw_thermal_slowdown=Active / temperature >= 85 C (WARN), or dmesg 'Detected insufficient power on the PCIe slot (27W)' (CRIT)
candidate_rules.evidence_template: nvidia-smi sample: power {p} W, util {u}%, sm {clk} MHz, temp {t} C, sw_thermal_slowdown={thr}. Spec: GPU max 120 W, system 240 W PSU.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Thermal capping halves sustained throughput; the 27 W PD defect needs RMA; the 5 W state is a driver bug fixed by 580.x/CUDA 13.
next_steps: sudo apt dist-upgrade; sudo fwupdmgr refresh && sudo fwupdmgr update
Improve airflow / ambient < 25 C; consider nvidia-smi -lgc 200,2150 to avoid firmware shutdowns
If 27W PCIe message present, contact NVIDIA support (hardware)

candidate_rules.trigger: Inference container lacks --ipc=host or --shm-size >= 16g, or TRT-LLM/vLLM container lacks --ulimit memlock=-1, or uses a mutable :latest tag
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Container {name} ({image}): IpcMode={ipc} ShmSize={shm} Ulimits={ulimits}. NVIDIA/LMSYS Spark recipes use --ipc=host, --shm-size 32g, --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Small /dev/shm breaks multi-process engines; memlock limits break pinned allocations; :latest may lack sm_121 kernels.
next_steps: docker run --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size 32g --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 ...
Pin image tags (e.g. nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.05-py3, lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130 -> a dated tag)

candidate_rules.trigger: User selects a dense model > 30B params for interactive/agent use with single-stream decode target > 10 tok/s
candidate_rules.evidence_template: {model} {quant}: {w_gib} GiB weights -> bandwidth-bound ceiling ~{ceil} tok/s at 273 GB/s (measured: Llama 3.1 70B FP8 2.7 tok/s; Qwen3.8-27B FP8 8.2 tok/s). MoE alternatives: gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 ~50-60 tok/s, Nemotron 3 Super 120B NVFP4 ~23-38 tok/s, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B ~50-80 tok/s.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Decode reads every active weight per token; dense 70B at 4-bit is capped near 7 tok/s regardless of engine.
next_steps: Prefer MoE with 3-15B active params for interactive latency
Use speculative decoding (MTP/EAGLE3) where available (+80-100%)
Reserve dense 70B for batch/offline jobs with high concurrency

candidate_rules.trigger: MemAvailable < planned footprint but MemAvailable + (Cached + Buffers) >= footprint; or graphical.target active before a > 80 GiB load
candidate_rules.evidence_template: MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB, page cache {cache_gib} GiB, desktop session active ({target}). Dropping caches / headless mode frees ~{free_gib} GiB.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Page cache from prior model files and GNOME (2-3 GB) delay or block loads and disable vLLM auto-prefetch.
next_steps: sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' before loading
sudo systemctl set-default multi-user.target for headless serving
sudo sysctl vm.dirty_bytes=268435456

candidate_rules.trigger: Agent profile (coding agent / NemoClaw / RAG) with context budget < 32K tokens, or KV not sized for (1 + subagents) x context
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Agent workload '{agent}' with ctx={ctx} parallel={par}: KV {kv_gib} GiB. NVIDIA guidance: agents commonly use 30K-120K contexts; four subagents at 32K cost ~2.6x wall time; Ollama default context is 4096.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Coding agents fail or thrash with small contexts; vLLM --max-num-seqs and Ollama OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL must cover concurrent tool calls.
next_steps: vLLM: --max-model-len 65536-131072, --max-num-seqs 4, --enable-prefix-caching (default), --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser <model>
Ollama: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 (or num_ctx), OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2-4, OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1, OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0
llama.cpp: -c 65536 --jinja -fa on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 -np 2

candidate_rules.trigger: NemoClaw/OpenShell present but node < 22.16, daemon.json lacks default-cgroupns-mode host, or ports 18789/8080/8000 conflict
candidate_rules.evidence_template: node {node_ver}; /etc/docker/daemon.json default-cgroupns-mode={mode}; cgroup fs {cgfs}; listeners on 18789/8080/8000: {owners}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: OpenShell embeds k3s in Docker; on cgroup v2 without host cgroupns kubelet fails ('Failed to start ContainerManager...').

Install Node 22: curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | sudo -E bash -
Verify inference: curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models

candidate_rules.trigger: Driver major version 590 detected with vLLM in use; or kernel < 6.17.1 with large GGUF loads
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Driver {drv}, kernel {kernel}. Community report: driver 590.x CUDAGraph capture deadlock on GB10; kernel 6.17.1 NO_PAGE_MAPCOUNT needed for fast llama.cpp model loading.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Known-good stack per NVIDIA playbooks is DGX OS 7.x, driver 580.x, CUDA 13.0.
next_steps: Stay on 580.x until vLLM confirms 590 fix, or run vLLM with --enforce-eager as a workaround
Use --no-mmap for llama.cpp on older kernels

commands_and_flags.context: Windows on Arm (RTX Spark) toolchain notes
commands_and_flags.command: CUDA Toolkit 13.4 developer preview (Windows 11 ARM64); llama.cpp must be built with clang-cl; GeForce driver 616.00 Arm64 developer preview
commands_and_flags.notes: Compute capability and unified-memory reporting APIs for N1X not yet published; wizard should gate on driver >= 616 and PCI DEV_2E03/2E06.

open_questions: Exact bytes/param for GGUF Q4_K_M / UD-Q4_K_XL (~0.6 B/param) was not confirmed from a primary source; use measured file sizes (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_XL 16.68 GB for 27B = 0.62 B/param) until verified.

Nemotron-3-Super KV/state cost per token: attention KV is ~8 KiB/token (8 attention layers x 2 kv heads x 128 x 2 x 2 B) but Frank Denneman measured ~7 GB per Ollama parallel slot at 262K, implying Mamba state + buffers dominate; the wizard needs a per-architecture 'state' term for hybrid Mamba models (Nemotron 3/3.5, Qwen3.8 Gated DeltaNet).

gpt-oss sliding-window layers (sliding_window 128 on alternating layers) mean real KV is roughly half the full-attention upper bound; confirm how vLLM/llama.cpp actually allocate for hybrid SWA models before using the smaller number.

Whether DGX OS 7.x ships with swap or zram enabled by default was not confirmed (community guides tell users to run swapoff -a, and LMSYS suggested enabling swap for gpt-oss-120b stability in Oct 2025); the wizard should detect rather than assume.
Precise OS/firmware reservation on current DGX OS 7.3.x: sources disagree between ~119 GiB and ~121.7 GiB MemTotal and 3-7 GB OS baseline; measure at runtime.

vLLM's exact runtime/JIT overhead on GB10 varies widely by version (3 GB runtime + 13 GB compile/graphs in one report; ~50 GB transient kernel-init allocation in another with nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.07-py3); the wizard should use a conservative 15 GiB reserve and re-measure MemAvailable after startup.

Whether the NVFP4 kernel gap on sm_121 (no cvt.e2m1x2; Marlin fallback) still applies in vLLM >= 0.26 / NGC 26.05+; the vLLM team's June 2026 post serves NVFP4 Nemotron at 22.7-23.7 tok/s while Kubesimplify reports ~38 tok/s, suggesting kernel paths differ by build.
Driver 590.x CUDAGraph deadlock on GB10 is a single-source community report (eugr README); needs confirmation before making it a WARN rule.

RTX Spark (N1X) specifics are unpublished: compute capability (likely sm_12x), Windows unified-memory reporting (nvidia-smi/NVML vs GlobalMemoryStatusEx), whether Ollama/LM Studio ship Arm64 CUDA builds at launch, WSL2 CUDA support, and real sustained bandwidth (press says ~300 GB/s) and 45-80 W thermal behavior under decode.

Ollama's published DGX Spark blog (prefill/decode numbers cited by Kubesimplify: Llama 3.1 8B Q4 7,614/38, gpt-oss-20b 3,224/58, DeepSeek R1 14B Q4 5,919/20) could not be fetched directly (404 at guessed URLs); treat as medium confidence.

Qwen3-235B-A22B NVFP4 on a single Spark: NVIDIA's TRT-LLM playbook lists nvidia/Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP4 as multi-node only; at ~0.56 B/param the ~133B-param checkpoint is ~70-75 GB and might fit single-node with small context, but no single-Spark tokens/s number was found.
